study_name.notes: Study name inferred from paper title and publication context; no explicit study name provided in the paper.

target_condition.evidence_quote: characterized the gut microbiome of the Yanomami from Brazil and compared taxonomically and functionally
target_condition.notes: Primary focus is characterization of gut microbiome in hunter-gatherer populations.

control.notes: US group serves as comparison/control group; other groups are case/study groups. Study is observational, not case-control designed.

country.evidence_quote: The Yanomami is the largest indigenous semi-isolated group in the Amazon to maintain traditional subsistence practices based on hunting, fishing, gathering, and swidden horticulture. They inhabit the Amazon region encompassing the Brazil and Venezuela border
country.notes: Country varies by subgroup; Matses and Tunapuco from Peruvian Amazon per citations.

body_site.evidence_quote: Participants were requested to provide a morning fecal sample, and a labeled screw-capped plastic container was provided. A single stool sample was collected
body_site.section: Materials and Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection

lifestyle.evidence_quote: two hunter–gatherer communities [Yanomami from Venezuela, n = 8; Matses, n = 24], a rural agricultural community [Tunapuco, n = 12]
lifestyle.notes: Tunapuco explicitly identified as rural agricultural community; Yanomami and Matses as hunter-gatherer communities.

location.evidence_quote: the Matses from the Peruvian Amazon (n = 24), the Tunapuco from the Andean highlands (n = 12); and a representative group of urban individuals from the United States (n = 44)
location.section: Results — Intra- and Inter-Individual Diversity of the Gut Microbiomes

westernized.evidence_quote: traditional groups from the Amazon; and an urban-industrialized group
westernized.notes: South American groups identified as traditional/non-westernized; US group identified as urban-industrialized.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Total DNA was extracted from 15 stool samples with FastDNA ® SPIN Kit (MP Biomedicals)
dna_extraction_kit.section: Materials and Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Applied only to Yanomami/Brazil samples (n=15). Other groups' data from published sources without extraction details provided here.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified libraries were sequenced on a HiSeq ® 2500 sequencer (Oswaldo Cruz Foundation, high-throughput sequencing platform)
sequencing_platform.section: Materials and Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
sequencing_platform.notes: Applied to Yanomami/Brazil samples. Other groups sequenced on Illumina platforms per bioinformatic processing section.

age.evidence_quote: At the time of the collection, age and gender information of the individuals were also acquired. These details are summarized in Supplementary Table 1
age.section: Materials and Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
age.notes: Age data collected but not reported in main text; referenced as in Supplementary Table 1, which is not provided.

age_unit.notes: Age data not provided in extracted sections.

sex.evidence_quote: Association between gut microbiome composition and gender was analyzed with principal coordinate analysis (PcoA) generated with Bray–Curtis distances. These comparisons did not reveal any statistically significant differences in the gut microbiome of female and male Yanomami/Brazil individuals
sex.section: Results — Intra- and Inter-Individual Diversity of the Gut Microbiomes
sex.notes: Paper mentions gender/sex data were collected but specific individual sex values not reported; only comparative analysis stated.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Escherichia and Ralstonia genera in the Yanomami/Brazil, and therefore, they were defined as Yanomami/Brazil biomarkers. On the other hand, Neisseria and Desulfovibrio were defined as Yanomami/Venezuela biomarkers, while Klebsiella was the biomarker of the Matses group.
biomarker_name.notes: Biomarkers identified for different groups include bacterial genera (taxa) and functional gene families. The list includes taxonomic biomarkers (genera from bacterial phyla) and functional biomarkers (metabolic pathways and functions).

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Barplot representing the relative abundance (percentage) of the most frequent phyla in the gut microbiomes.
biomarker_unit.notes: Biomarkers are reported as relative abundance (percentage) or as gene family classifications from SEED database.

biomarker_value.notes: The paper identifies biomarkers qualitatively (presence/absence and taxonomic assignment) but does not provide specific quantitative values (e.g., percentage abundances) for individual biomarkers in tabular form. Relative abundances are discussed descriptively but not numerically specified for each biomarker.

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Shannon index of alpha-diversity was estimated for each metagenome. Beta-diversity was determined using Bray–Curtis dissimilarity and permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) was performed with 999 permutations.
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiome phenotypes measured include diversity metrics (alpha and beta diversity), taxonomic composition (phyla and genera), and functional profiles from metagenomic analysis.

value: Study population: Yanomami hunter-gatherer group from Brazil (n=15) and Venezuela (n=8), Matses from Peru (n=24), Tunapuco from Andes highlands (n=12), US urban individuals (n=44)
Sequencing method: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing on HiSeq 2500 generating ~14 million reads per sample
Taxonomic classification: Kraken using NCBI whole genome database; bacteria and archaea identified
Functional classification: SUPER-FOCUS using SEED database gene families and subsystems
Statistical methods: Kruskal-Wallis test (alpha=0.05), LDA score >4.0, PERMANOVA with 999 permutations, Wilcoxon rank-sum test
Key finding: Yanomami/Brazil microbiome distinguished by higher abundance of regulation/cell signaling, motility/chemotaxis, and virulence gene families
Environmental factor: Cadmium contamination possible from battery discharge in Yanomami/Brazil area
Diet characterization: Low in fat and salt, high in fruits, fiber, and sylvatic animals
Ethics approval: Oswaldo Cruz Foundation Ethics Committee No. 638/11 and CONEP No. 16907
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Total DNA was extracted from 15 stool samples with FastDNA SPIN Kit. Metagenomic libraries were constructed with TruSeq DNA Sample Preparation v2 Kit following the standard protocols. Purified libraries were sequenced on a HiSeq 2500 sequencer producing a total of ~219 million reads, with an average of ~14 million reads per sample.
uncurated_metadata.section: Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
uncurated_metadata.notes: Additional metadata includes study design, sequencing and analytical methods, sample sizes for each group, and contextual information about lifestyle and environment.

host_species.evidence_quote: The Yanomami is the largest semi-nomadic hunter–gatherer group of the Americas, exploring different niches of the Amazon rainforest in Brazil and Venezuela.
host_species.notes: The study explicitly focuses on human participants (Yanomami indigenous group, US urban population). Species is inferred as Homo sapiens based on the human study participants described throughout.
